app_summary: An online shop selling astronomy products, based on the OpenTelemetry Demo. It is built with polyglot microservices (Go, Java, .NET, Python, Node.js, Rust, ...) communicating via gRPC and HTTP behind an Envoy frontend-proxy, with Kafka for asynchronous order processing and Valkey as cart store. Supported Operations: View product catalog, Receive product recommendations and ads, Add item to cart, Checkout with selected items, Currency conversion, Process payment, Generate shipping quotes, Send order confirmation emails

final_report.root_cause: INCONCLUSIVE — conflicting evidence. Traces show a proxy loop pattern (frontend-proxy appears as both caller and callee, often via image-provider) causing ~10s latencies, but cluster configuration and frontend-proxy runtime logs do not show a routing misconfiguration or runtime loop. Two plausible explanations remain: (A) a true Envoy routing loop (requests forwarded back to the proxy) that was not visible in the inspected pod logs (access logs not emitted to stdout) or (B) tracing/instrumentation misattribution where spans from multiple components are labeled 'frontend-proxy' (or service names are duplicated), producing an apparent loop in traces while no actual loop exists. Additional targeted data is required to distinguish these and produce a final root-cause statement.
final_report.evidence_summary: 1) Traces: Multiple recent traces (~30 slow traces) show ~10,000 ms end-to-end latency and sequences where frontend-proxy appears both as caller and callee (e.g., 'frontend-proxy -> image-provider -> frontend-proxy' and 'frontend-web -> frontend-proxy -> frontend -> frontend-proxy'). This is the primary symptom pointing at a proxy loop. 2) Cluster config: frontend-proxy Deployment env vars point to IMAGE_PROVIDER_HOST=image-provider:8081; image-provider Service is a ClusterIP (10.96.246.13) with endpoints pointing to the image-provider pod (10.244.1.32:8081). No evidence the Service or endpoints resolve to the frontend-proxy. 3) image-provider Deployment has no CALLBACK/BASE_URL env vars, no ConfigMap references, and no indication it should call the proxy back. 4) frontend-proxy pod logs show Envoy startup and cluster initialization but no access-log lines or WARN/ERROR entries indicating routing errors, no healthy/upstream failures, and no loop detection; possible explanation is that access logs are not being emitted to stdout where they were fetched. 5) No ConfigMap with Envoy bootstrap config was found to inspect for baked-in misroutes (Envoy config appears baked into the container or driven by env vars). These findings conflict: traces indicate a loop, but service discovery/config and pod logs do not provide corroboration.
final_report.investigation_summary: Priority-1 trace analysis identified the loop pattern in multiple representative traces and concluded a routing loop in frontend-proxy could explain the ~10s latencies. Priority-2 and -3 inspections of Kubernetes resources (Deployments/Services) showed that DNS/ClusterIP for image-provider resolved to the image-provider pod and that image-provider has no config pointing to the frontend-proxy, reducing the likelihood of a Service selector misconfiguration or application-level callback causing the loop. Priority-4 pod log inspection of frontend-proxy found normal Envoy initialization but no access/log evidence of request-level proxying or loops; however access logs may not be emitted to stdout, so the log absence is not definitive. Because trace evidence and cluster/runtime evidence conflict, we cannot conclusively localize the failure to a specific component without further targeted data.
